thread.title: Can Apple End Its Losing Streak? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Can Apple End Its Losing Streak? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Next week, all eyes will be on Apple ( AAPL ) at its WorldWide Developers Conference ("WWDC"). This annual event is mostly used to show off the company's newest operating systems, but sometimes we see new products. While this event is always a glimpse into Apple's future, there always are high expectations going in. Perhaps that's what makes it the stock's worst week of the year generally.
This year, MacRumors compiled an extensive list of readers' wishes for iOS 12, and I'm sure not all of these features will come to light. Apple will certainly make improvements for the iPhone and iPad, but not everyone will be satisfied. Usually, however, the biggest expectations involve the potential for new products, some of which can be seen below.
This year, we expect to see new versions of iOS, macOS, tvOS, and watchOS at the conference, and it's possible Apple also will use the event to unveil new iPad Pro models and new Macs. Apple is rumored to be working on an updated iPad Pro that features an iPhone X-style edge-to-edge display with no Home button and support for Face ID. It's not clear, however, if this device will be ready to debut at WWDC as rumors have said that it may not come until later in the year. Apple often introduces refreshed Macs, and the iMac, MacBook Pro, and MacBook are all awaiting 2018 refreshes. It's also possible Apple will use the WWDC event to launch the long-awaited AirPower, a charging mat that's designed to charge the iPhone X, 8 and 8 Plus models at the same time as AirPods (with a new charging case) and the Apple Watch Series 3. Ask a large enough number of investors or Apple enthusiasts , and I'm sure you'll see expectations for every product line to have something new unveiled at WWDC. There are even rumors of a new iPhone SE and possibly HomePod coming at the event. As product expectations pile up, it only increases the chance for disappointment, so when Apple doesn't release a ton of shiny new gadgets, the stock tends to sell off.
Last year, WWDC was a pretty good showing in terms of products. The HomePod was unveiled, although it didn't go on sale for quite a while, while a new iPad Pro and iMac Pro were shown off. They key takeaway in 2017 was that Apple was not afraid to move up the price ladder with these new products, and we continued to see that later in the year with the iPhone 8/X launch.
While unit sales have not been that impressive in recent quarters for some devices, total revenues have been decent thanks to higher average selling prices. While this scenario works with strong global economies, consumers may eventually push back if prices continue rising.
As you can see in the table below, the week of WWDC usually means a lot of red for the stock. Since 2001, the only WWDC week that Apple shares finished higher was in 2014, and that was a unique time because investors piled into the stock right before the 7 for 1 stock split. Of the 16 weeks that shares have declined, the average loss has been 3.86%, basically the average of the last two years as well.
( Data sourced from Yahoo! Finance. *WWDC was right before split)
So as everyone looks to see what Apple unveils next week at WWDC, I'll be watching the stock to see if it can end its losing streak. We will definitely see the new bells and whistles of Apple's upgraded operating systems, but are we going to see any new hardware unveiled? As usual, expectations for new devices are rather high, making it hard for the company to satisfy everyone. That's what makes it a tough week for the stock.
